title: Being remembered for Condon's records around the world
summary: Fans in Europe and everywhere thank him for the Condon records, which have been reissued, and he says whether it was a peak is a matter of taste.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: ---and every visiting fireman from across America--- who used to come in to Condon's This-- just to give an example of that - why don't you tell a little bit about your travels around the country and what happens when just about every place you go - all kinds of people come up and say - I heard you play in Condon's---
Even, here it is, 25 years later.

And, today, when I play Europe and you know, I play all over the world now, I never play a place that guys don't come and say - well, thank you for Eddie Condon's and we've started our band from your style-- of records and--- to this day and this is thirty someting years later, they have never forgotten me because you know the records have been re-released again.
Like Jamming at Condon's, Condon's Coast to Coast.

Yeah - I made all those and they had become very famous and people, for a long time before Ed died, people were looking for those things to be released again because they worn their records out and you couldn't buy them anymore. And, now, they're being released again.
A lot of people think that this may have been-the Condon years - may have been the high point in jazz in this country; a lot of people think that.
Well, I think, on the other hand, it's what you like.
You know, some people like that and I've people say that that wasn't jazz too. So--- what the hell are you going to do. Well, I think we should just rest here for a minute---
